text.text: Turkish has two question types. Yes/no questions are formed with the clitic

, which is written as a separate word and must harmonise with the last vowel of the word before it. The clitic follows the focused word — usually the predicate — and carries the person ending in nominal and present-tense predicates (except 3rd-person plural -lAr, which stays before mI: geliyorlar mı?). In the past tense with
, the person ending stays on the verb and
is left bare. Content (WH) questions use question words such as

in place of the unknown element; these words normally stand in the same position the answer word would occupy, rather than being moved to the front the way English WH-words are. When nothing else comes before it, the WH-word is simply first: Nerede oturuyorsun?

Use mI after a noun or adjective predicate when asking whether someone or something belongs to a category. The person ending moves from the predicate onto mI (3rd-person plural -lAr stays: öğrenciler mi?).
Use mI after the present-tense verb stem + tense suffix. The person ending attaches to mI, not to the verb — except 3rd-person plural -lAr, which stays on the verb (geliyorlar mı?).
The person ending stays on the verb. mI follows the fully inflected verb and carries no extra ending.

Replace the unknown element with the appropriate question word. No mI clitic is used. The question word occupies the same slot as the answer would.
The form of mI is determined by four-way vowel harmony based on the last vowel of the preceding word.

text.text: In the past tense the person ending stays on the verb.

. The mI clitic in past-tense questions carries no person ending.

A quick rule of thumb: in the -dı past, the verb is already fully inflected before mI arrives. In all other tenses and in nominal predicates, mI takes the person ending — except 3rd-person plural -lAr, which always comes before mI (geliyorlar mı?).
